subcategory: evidence restructuring into reasoning chains to transfer reasoning-model strategies to non-reasoning LLMs
problem: Reasoning LLMs improve multi-hop RAG but at high token and latency cost; their benefit comes from implicit strategies (context-grounded vs knowledge-reconciled reasoning) that non-reasoning models lack.
architecture: LiR3AG: after an empirical study of Qwen3 'think' traces, a lightweight framework re-ranks and restructures retrieved evidence into coherent reasoning chains (intermediate components on GPT-4o-mini) so that a non-reasoning 8B generator can follow the transferred strategy.
retriever: standard dense retrieval of top-k passages
generator: Qwen3-8B (no-think); Qwen3-14B/32B baselines; GPT-4o-mini for intermediate modules
knowledge_source: corpora of the multi-hop QA benchmarks
key_results: Qwen3-8B no-think with LiR3AG: HotpotQA F1 0.521 vs 0.501 for Vanilla RAG with Qwen3-32B think; MuSiQue F1 0.464 vs 0.410.
Reduces output tokens by 98% on average and inference time by 58.6% relative to reasoning models.
F1 of the 8B non-reasoning model improves by 6.2% to 22.5% across datasets.
strengths: Empirical characterisation of how reasoning models use retrieved vs internal knowledge in RAG.
Large efficiency gains with a small generator.

limitations.text: Compared only with Direct Output and Vanilla RAG, not with more complex RAG methods.
Intermediate modules use GPT-4o-mini, so the cost of these calls partly offsets the savings on the generator.

title: LiR3AG: A Lightweight Rerank Reasoning Strategy Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
